assistant_id.description: Set on a Space Assistant's conversation, which continues only in its chat; user_id is then the requester.

checks.description: Every dependency probed. An empty array means nothing was verified.

name.description: Which dependency, never where it lives

sandboxed.description: False means nothing confined the run's Bash commands

sources.description: Layer chain that decided the boundary, e.g. default:worker, settings, policy

TraceMCP.description: How the run's MCP transports were treated. Absent means the trace predates this record — unknown, not stdio-allowed.

stdio_disabled.description: The unattended-worker profile refused stdio MCP for this run

remote_transports.description: Resolved remote transport kinds active for the run, a sorted subset of http and sse

path.description: The call's file_path argument, when it had one

run_id.description: Agent run id; also the trace file's name

tools_truncated.description: The tools list was bounded; tool_calls still counts them all

workspace.description: What happened to this run's workspace checkpoint: whether it restored a base and whether it committed a result.

error.description: Terminal error; empty when the run succeeded

user_kind.description: service marks a Space-owned service account, which people pickers leave out.

AssistantRosterEntry.description: An Agent or published Workflow an Assistant may dispatch, with its release contract: the result shape and which top-level fields may reach a requester. An Agent entry declares output_schema; a Workflow entry uses its result node's.

AssistantStatement.description: What publishing an Assistant discloses: who can ask, what it can read and run, and the Secrets that work can use. Confirming its digest is how an owner publishes it.

AssistantDefinition.description: The whole definition a create or edit proposes. An omitted service_account_id on create makes a service account with the Assistant's name.

Assistant.description: A Space Assistant: a service front door the Space publishes on its own chat bot. See docs/design/space-assistants.md.

availability.description: Whether it answers now. An active Assistant pauses on its own while its service account is disabled or it lacks a valid sponsor.

binding.description: Its bot, never with the token.

AssistantStatementRequired.description: The 409 for publishing, or widening an active Assistant, without confirming the current statement. Send its digest back as confirm_statement.

ServiceAccount.description: A Space-owned service account: a non-human principal work runs as, accountable through a human sponsor. It has no email and no credential. See docs/design/space-assistants.md §6.

needs_sponsor.description: True when the sponsor is missing, disabled, or no longer an owner or admin of the Space. Cleared by re-sponsoring to an owner or admin.

Invitation.description: A pending offer of space membership against an account that already exists. Never carries a code -- see docs/design/space-membership-lifecycle.md.

conversation_id.description: Set on an issue a Space Assistant escalated: the chat conversation it came from.

assistant_id.description: The Space Assistant that escalated this issue.

requested_by.description: The person who asked the Space Assistant; answer them with requester-replies.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency token; PATCH must send the version it read

RunIssue.description: The bounded view of an issue a run's agent reads. Not the full issue: children are title and status only, and the comment thread is a recent window.

omitted_comments.description: How many older comments the window left out

author_kind.description: "agent" is a run this deployment scheduled and recorded. "local_agent" is an agent on someone's own machine, reported over their session — a claim, not something the deployment observed.

author_id.description: A user_id, or an agent_id for "agent". For "local_agent" it is the person who reported it

input.description: The run's immutable input, validated against the workflow input_schema.

result.description: The run's declared result, resolved from a node output when the run succeeded.

status.description: failing/canceling retain live TaskRuns until their workers stop.

failure_class.description: Why the run failed, recorded when it started failing; absent for a run that has not failed.

deadline_at.description: When the run fails if unfinished, from the definition's policy.timeout_seconds; absent when none is set.

input.description: The run's immutable input, validated against the workflow input_schema.

result.description: The run's declared result, resolved from a node output when the run succeeded; present only when the definition declares a result selector.

attempt.description: Attempts admitted so far; 0 before dispatch. task_run_id is always the latest attempt's run.

max_attempts.description: The node's attempt budget, first attempt included.

timeout_seconds.description: Per-attempt timeout; absent when the node has none.

deadline_at.description: When the current attempt times out.

next_attempt_at.description: When a retry_wait node admits its next attempt.

prompt.description: What a human_input step asks, with its bound values.

questions.description: The questions a step's Agent asked, for kind question.

response_schema.description: The JSON Schema an answer must satisfy; absent means free text.

task_run_id.description: The attempt that asked, for kind question.

response.description: The answer, or a decline's reason as a string.

managed_calls.description: The caller's own managed calls from signed-in CLI and Desktop sessions over the same period. They belong to no space, so the space figures do not include them. Returned only by GET /api/usage, and only on a deployment with a call ledger.

costs.description: One entry per currency, in nano-units; never summed across currencies.

QuotaTier.description: A seeded tier's limits. Zero max_storage_bytes means no storage limit; period_days does not apply to storage.

sponsor_user_id.description: The accountable owner or admin of a service account.

get.description: Reports that the process is running. Checks no dependencies by design — a liveness probe that failed on a dependency outage would restart a healthy server.

Reports whether the server can serve traffic, probing each configured dependency. Names the failing check but never the reason, which goes to the server log: this endpoint is unauthenticated and connection errors carry DSNs and endpoints.

Unauthenticated: a client has to know how to sign in before it can. Reports the effective `local_login` mode (`all`, `system_admins`, or `off`) and whether SSO is offered with its display name. It never carries the issuer, client id, or provisioning policy.
Mints a login transaction (state, nonce, PKCE) bound to the browser in a short-lived cookie and redirects to the IdP's authorize endpoint. Answers 404 when SSO is not configured.

Verifies the transaction cookie and state, exchanges the code, validates the ID Token, associates the account, opens a session, and sets the Portal refresh cookie before redirecting to the Portal. On failure it redirects to the sign-in page with a coarse, non-sensitive `?sso_error=` class (unavailable, expired, not_authorized, disabled); no token, email, or raw provider error is ever in the URL.

302.description: Redirect to the Portal on success, or to the sign-in page with an sso_error class on failure

post.description: Accepts either a `password` (the everyday credential) or a single-use `otp` login code (the recovery path, issued by an operator). Returns an access token and, when the deployment stores them, a refresh token. `token` repeats `access_token` under the name it had before the two were split.

post.summary: Set or change the caller's password
post.description: Requires the current password when the account already has one: a session by itself must not be enough, since a stolen access token works until its session is revoked or expires. Setting the first password after signing in with a login code needs no current password.

400.description: New password fails the length rule, or body invalid

401.description: Not authenticated, or the current password is wrong

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair
post.description: Unauthenticated: possession of the refresh token is the proof. Each exchange spends the token presented and returns its replacement in the same session. Presenting a spent token past `refresh_rotation_grace` revokes the whole session.

400.description: refresh_token missing, or body invalid

401.description: Token unknown, expired, revoked, or reused

503.description: Deployment has no refresh token store

post.description: Accepts either credential: a refresh_token in the body names its session, otherwise the session comes from the access token's sid claim. Revoking a session the server has already forgotten is a success.

503.description: Deployment has no refresh token store

post.description: Same credential check as `/api/auth/login`, but the renewable credential is set as a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to `/api/auth/portal` instead of returned in the body. The response carries only the short-lived access token and the user. Requires a same-origin `Origin`.

400.description: Body invalid

403.description: Account disabled, or cross-origin request

post.summary: Exchange the Portal refresh cookie for an access token
post.description: Reads the refresh cookie, rotates it, and returns a fresh access token and the user. The Portal calls it on load, on reload, and on a 401. A missing or dead cookie is a 401 and the cookie is cleared. Requires a same-origin `Origin`.

401.description: No cookie, or the session is no longer active

403.description: Cross-origin request

post.description: Revokes the session the refresh cookie names and clears the cookie. An absent cookie is still a success. Requires a same-origin `Origin`.

403.description: Cross-origin request

get.summary: List the models this deployment offers for managed inference
get.description: Being signed in is the whole authorization: the catalog is deployment-global, so every enabled model is available to every user. Identity is resolved before the gateway is touched, so an unauthenticated caller learns nothing about whether this deployment offers managed inference. Each model carries its current pricing when the operator set one, as decimal strings per million tokens, so a client prices its own session the way the call ledger does.

Unknown request fields are rejected rather than ignored. With stream=true the response is text/event-stream carrying delta, result, and error events. A foreground call is attributed to the caller and metered against no space.
